newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: German chemical giant maps out Asian future.
newsitem.headline: German chemical giant maps out Asian future.

text.p: German chemicals giant BASF AG has targeted three Asian sites outside Japan for development of integrated production facilities, at a cost of several billion German marks, a senior company official said.
In a weekend interview with Reuters, Volker Trautz, a BASF executive directors, identified these as Nanjing in China, Mangalore in India and most probably Kuantan in Malaysia.
"Our main objective outside of Japan is to transfer one of our special core competencies by building up three production sites with world-scale plants to serve the regions," Trautz said.
Through these investments BASF hopes to double its market share in Asia, generating at least 20 percent of its sales and group earnings.
In 1995, BASF sales were at 46.2 billion marks and pre-tax profits at 4.13 billion marks.
Although the company is moving the global headquarters of its textile and leather dyes and chemicals division to Singapore, no investments are planned on the island.

This is the first time BASF has moved a division headquarters to Asia, although it has two other divisions based outside Germany -- the fibers unit in North America and the polyuretane unit in Belgium.
"We are a little bit late in Singapore. If it were 10 years ago it would be totally different," he said.

BASF was not among the core companies that had got together to build Singapore's first petrochemical complex in the early eighties, but its subsequent venture to invest in a second complex will start up early next year.
"We are not very happy with the situation," Trautz.
But BASF is seen as a pioneer investor in the development of Malaysia's chemical sector in Kuantan in eastern Pahang state.

The company recently signed a letter of intent with state-owned oil company Petronas to build its first acrylic monomer plant in Asia for $250 million. The plant, with a yearly capacity of 160,000 tonnes, is to be completed by end-1999.
Acrylic monomers are raw materials for the production of polymer dispersions, used in paints and coatings, and in superabsorbers, which help make hygiene products like nappies.
Trautz said projects for production of other basic chemicals such as oxo alcohols and propylene are being considered.

In China, BASF has mapped out an ambitious 6 billion mark (US$3.9 billion) investment plan at the heart of which is a 600,000 tonne per year naphtha cracker for production of ethylene, a basic petrochemical used to make plastics.
The integrated project, a joint venture with state-owned Sinopec and Yangzi Petrochemical, is located in Nanjing on the Yangtze river.
BASF will begin production of up to 120,000 tonnes per year of styrene and polystryene at a neighbouring site in mid-1997.
Tautz said discussions in China are more advanced than forn the other two sites as a detailed five-year plan was already sent to the authorities.
In Mangalore, India, BASF currently has plants for production of textile and leather dyes and polymer dispersions for textile and industry.
Trautz said a plastic plant is BASF's most likely next investment in India.
